steps.scene: On a three-lane motorway you've just passed a lorry in the middle lane. The left-hand lane ahead is empty for as far as you can see.

question.prompt: Which lane should you be in now?

options.text: The middle lane — it's the normal cruising lane
The left-hand lane
Whichever lane you're in — stay put until your exit

question.explanation: You've finished overtaking, so move back left. Sitting in the middle lane holds up everyone behind you.

steps.title: The lanes to your right
steps.body: Lanes to the right are for overtaking. When you're past, move back left — without cutting in front of the vehicle you've just overtaken.

question.prompt: On a three-lane motorway, what's the right-hand lane there for?

options.text: When you're travelling at 70 mph
When you're turning right at the next junction
When you're overtaking

question.explanation: There's no fast lane. The lanes to your right exist so you can pass — then you move back left.

a.label: Traffic flowing freely
a.body: Never overtake on the left. Pass slower vehicles only on their right.

b.label: Slow-moving queues
b.body: If the queue to your right is moving more slowly than yours, you may keep going past it in your lane.

question.prompt: When may you pass traffic on its left on a motorway?

options.text: Whenever the lane to the left is clear
In queues, when traffic to your right is moving more slowly
When the driver ahead won't move over

question.explanation: Drivers don't expect to be passed on the left. The only exception is queuing traffic moving at different speeds.

steps.scene: You're in the left-hand lane approaching a junction. Several cars are speeding up the slip road to join just ahead of you.

options.text: Hold your speed — they have to give way to you
Speed up so they have to join behind you
Adjust your speed, or move out a lane if it's safe

question.explanation: Joining traffic must give way, but you can make it easier. Planning ahead keeps the whole flow moving.

steps.scene: The traffic ahead brakes hard to a stop around a bend. Fast traffic is coming up behind you.

question.prompt: How can you warn the drivers behind you?

options.text: Briefly switch on your hazard warning lights
You can't — hazard lights are only for breakdowns
Flash your headlights

question.explanation: On a motorway or dual carriageway you may use hazard lights briefly to warn of a hazard ahead. Switch them off once you've been seen.

steps.title: Towing on the motorway
steps.body: Towing a caravan or trailer drops your limit to 60 mph on motorways and dual carriageways — even where the cars around you can do 70.

question.prompt: You're towing a caravan on the motorway. What's your top speed?

options.text: 50 mph
70 mph, the same as any other car
60 mph

question.explanation: A trailer makes your vehicle longer, heavier and less stable, so the limit is lower.

steps.wrongBelief: The left-hand lane of a motorway is really for lorries and slow vehicles.

question.prompt: You're driving a small car at 70 mph and nothing's ahead. Which lane is yours?

options.text: Not the left — that's for lorries and slow vehicles
The left-hand lane
The middle lane, until you're near your exit

question.explanation: Keep left unless you're overtaking — whatever you're driving and however fast you're going.

steps.repairNote: The left-hand lane is everyone's lane. Use the others only to overtake, then move back.
